question: Should acpx permanently reserve the generic `pool` keyword as the built-in name for Poolside’s `pool acp` server?
rationale: The implementation is technically complete, but repository policy treats built-in names as stable product surface and current fallback behavior allows arbitrary commands to occupy that namespace.

options.title: Approve the `pool` built-in
options.body: Accept the official CLI name as a stable built-in alias, with existing explicit-command and configuration paths available for collisions.

options.title: Use a less generic alias
options.body: Ask the contributor to use a more product-specific built-in name such as `poolside`, accepting divergence from the upstream executable name to reduce namespace collision risk.

options.title: Keep Poolside configurable only
options.body: Close or decline the core alias while continuing to support Poolside through the existing custom command and agent configuration paths.

recommendation.title: Approve the `pool` built-in
recommendation.body: Accept the official CLI name as a stable built-in alias, with existing explicit-command and configuration paths available for collisions.

likelyOwner.reason: They most recently merged and maintained an equivalent built-in-agent registry addition and are best positioned to decide whether this keyword belongs in the stable core surface.
